introduction-why-engineers-must-write.core: Writing scales thinking: a well-written doc reaches hundreds of people asynchronously, forces clarity, persists beyond meetings and lets ideas be challenged on their merits. Senior engineering influence is largely written.

first_principles.problem: Great ideas die in meetings because they're never written clearly, and decisions are forgotten or re-litigated.
truths: Documents scale across time zones and time.
derivation: Write **strategy docs** with diagnosis, policy and actions.

analogy.title: A lawyer's brief
analogy.story: Brilliant oral arguments lose to a well-written brief that the judge can study.
analogy.breaks: Over-documenting trivial decisions is waste, so match the writing to the stakes.

example.title: A decision with and without a doc
flow: Meeting only: unclear outcome, re-debated in 3 months
RFC: reasoning recorded, comments resolved, decision linked forever

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The decision sticks and its context survives.

example.outcome: ideas that travel and decisions that last.

check.q: Why is writing especially important for senior engineers?
check.a: It scales their reasoning across many people and time, forces clarity, and preserves decisions.

the-narrative-amazons-6-pager.core: Amazon replaces slide decks with six-page narrative memos read silently at the start of meetings. Prose forces complete reasoning and connected arguments that bullet points let you skip.

first_principles.problem: Slide bullets hide gaps in logic, and presenters control the pace, so audiences don't engage deeply.
derivation: Include **context, problem, proposal, alternatives and risks**.

analogy.title: A novel vs. a list of plot points
analogy.story: 'Hero leaves, meets mentor, returns' tells you nothing about why; the novel explains.
analogy.breaks: Long narratives can be slow to write and read, so keep them focused.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The reasoning and the risks are visible.

code.text:
Bullet: • Migrate to Postgres • Cheaper • Q3
Narrative: "Our licensing costs rose 40% this year while usage grew 10%. Migrating to Postgres
removes the per-core licence, saving ~$400k annually. The main risk is stored-procedure
rewrites, which we mitigate by…"

check.q: Why does Amazon prefer narrative memos to slides?
check.a: Prose forces complete, connected reasoning, and silent reading gives everyone the same understanding before discussion.

the-rfc-process-engineering-democracy.core: An RFC (Request for Comments) is a written technical proposal shared for review before implementation: problem, proposal, alternatives, trade-offs, risks. Structured feedback and a clear decision owner give inclusive yet decisive design.

first_principles.problem: Big technical changes are decided in hallway conversations, which leaves teams surprised, concerns missed and decisions disputed.
derivation: Use a **template**: context, goals/non-goals, proposal, alternatives, risks, rollout.
Have a **review period** with named reviewers.
**Resolve comments** and record the decision (accepted or rejected).

analogy.title: A city planning public consultation
analogy.story: Plans are published, residents comment, the council decides, and the record is kept.
analogy.breaks: RFC processes can become slow bureaucracy, so time-box them and scale to the size of the decision.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Broad input, a clear decision, a durable record.

check.q: What should every RFC include besides the proposal itself?
check.a: Context, goals and non-goals, considered alternatives, trade-offs and risks.

the-strategy-document-avoiding-fluff.core: Good strategy (Rumelt) has a diagnosis of the challenge, a guiding policy for approaching it, and coherent actions. Bad strategy is fluff: vague goals ('be world class'), lists of wishes and no real choices.

first_principles.problem: 'Our strategy is to be the best platform with excellent reliability and velocity' tells nobody what to do or not do.
truths: A diagnosis must precede a solution.
derivation: **Guiding policy**: the overall approach (and what we won't do).
**Coherent actions**: concrete steps that fit together.

analogy.title: A doctor's treatment plan
analogy.story: Diagnosis (what's wrong), approach (surgery rather than medication) and specific actions (schedule, rehab).
analogy.breaks: Strategy must adapt as conditions change, so revisit it periodically.

example.title: A platform strategy kernel
flow: Diagnosis: 60% of eng time lost to infra toil across 40 teams
Policy: one paved road for stateless services; no bespoke infra
Actions: golden template, self-service DB, deprecate 3 legacy tools
example.outcome: strategy documents that guide real decisions.

check.q: What are the three elements of Rumelt's strategy kernel?
check.a: Diagnosis, guiding policy and coherent actions.
